question: Should upgrading silently remove legacy failed attachment queue records identified by the old stack-overflow error, or should this PR preserve them and land only the stack-safe parsing fix?
rationale: Those records contain persisted user messages and attachments; source inspection cannot determine whether maintainers prefer automatic cleanup over retaining a potentially retryable failed send.

options.title: Preserve legacy queue records
options.body: Remove the restore-time deletion rule and let users retry or explicitly discard old failed attachment messages after the parser fix.

options.title: Approve targeted automatic cleanup
options.body: Keep the version-marker migration and explicitly accept that matching pre-marker failed messages and attachments disappear during upgrade.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy queue records
recommendation.body: Remove the restore-time deletion rule and let users retry or explicitly discard old failed attachment messages after the parser fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The original WebSocket attachment contract traces to their implementation, making them the strongest available owner for the persisted-message compatibility choice.
